evals.prompt: Our Express + TypeScript API has top-level controllers/, services/, models/ and a 900-line utils.ts. We have orders, billing and users. Reorganize it.
evals.expected_output: Maps the current layout, proposes feature modules (orders, billing, users) each with entry-points/domain/data-access and a small public file, splits utils.ts into named helpers placed with their consumers or in libraries/, adds a boundary rule (no cycles, no deep imports) in CI, and plans an incremental migration one module per PR with moves separated from behavior changes.
expectations: Proposes organizing by feature or domain modules instead of top-level controllers/services/models
Splits utils.ts into concept-named files placed with their consumers or in a shared library folder
Adds an automated boundary check (e.g., dependency-cruiser or eslint rules) that runs in CI
Migrates incrementally, one module per PR, keeping file moves separate from behavior changes
Does not propose splitting into microservices

evals.prompt: Set up the folder structure for a new Go REST service with one API binary.
evals.expected_output: Uses the official go.dev module layout: go.mod at the root, a small main (in the root or cmd/api-server/ if a second binary is expected), domain packages under internal/, no pkg/ or empty scaffolding; notes that golang-standards/project-layout is not an official standard.
expectations: Puts non-public packages under internal/
Does not create a pkg/ directory or empty scaffolding folders such as api/, build/, deployments/
States or implies that golang-standards/project-layout is not an official Go standard
Names packages after what they provide rather than util/common

evals.prompt: Our React app is slow in dev and every feature folder has an index.ts that does export * from everything. Also features import each other all over the place. What should we do?
evals.expected_output: Explains the barrel-file cost (Vite guidance, bulletproof-react, Atlassian build speedup), recommends direct imports or small named public entries without export *, adds import/no-restricted-paths or eslint-plugin-boundaries zones to block cross-feature imports and enforce shared → features → app, and removes barrels incrementally with a codemod.
expectations: Recommends removing export * barrel files in favor of direct imports or a small explicit named public API
Cites a concrete reason or source for barrel cost (dev-server transform of all re-exported files, tree shaking, or build time)
Adds a lint rule that blocks cross-feature imports and enforces one-way shared to features to app dependencies
Proposes an incremental rollout rather than one big-bang change

evals.prompt: We're 3 developers starting a Next.js app. Should we set up an Nx monorepo with separate packages for ui, utils, and each feature, plus CODEOWNERS?
evals.expected_output: Stage 0-1 answer: a single Next.js app with feature folders and a shared ui folder; no monorepo tooling or per-feature packages until a second deployable or consumer exists; CODEOWNERS not needed yet; names the triggers for adopting each.
expectations: Recommends a single app with feature folders rather than a monorepo with per-feature packages
States that packages should be created only when a second consumer or deployable exists
Names at least one concrete trigger for adopting monorepo tooling or CODEOWNERS later
Advises against a utils package

evals.prompt: Should our payments module become its own microservice with its own database?
evals.expected_output: Near-miss: service extraction is a system-architecture decision; answers with the triggers (independent scaling, deploy cadence, isolation, runtime) and defers the extraction procedure to software-architecture rather than re-deriving folder layouts.
expectations: Asks for or lists concrete triggers for extracting a service (scaling, team ownership and deploy cadence, isolation or compliance, runtime)
Recommends enforcing the module boundary in-process before any extraction
Points to software-architecture for the extraction procedure
